nodes.name: entity
nodes.gloss: that which is perceived or known or inferred to have its own distinct existence (living or nonliving)

nodes.name: physical entity
nodes.gloss: an entity that has physical existence

nodes.name: abstraction
nodes.gloss: a general concept formed by extracting common features from specific examples

nodes.name: object
nodes.gloss: a tangible and visible entity; an entity that can cast a shadow; "it was full of rackets, balls and other objects"

nodes.name: whole
nodes.gloss: an assemblage of parts that is regarded as a single entity; "how big is that part compared to the whole?"; "the team is a unit"

nodes.name: living thing
nodes.gloss: a living (or once living) entity

nodes.name: organism
nodes.gloss: a living thing that has (or can develop) the ability to act or function independently

nodes.name: person
nodes.gloss: a human being; "there was too much for one person to do"

nodes.name: animal
nodes.gloss: a living organism characterized by voluntary movement

nodes.name: plant
nodes.gloss: (botany) a living organism lacking the power of locomotion

nodes.name: natural object
nodes.gloss: an object occurring naturally; not made by man

nodes.name: substance
nodes.gloss: the real physical matter of which a person or thing consists; "DNA is the substance of our genes"

nodes.name: substance
nodes.gloss: a particular kind or species of matter with uniform properties; "shigella is one of the most toxic substances known to man"

nodes.name: matter
nodes.gloss: that which has mass and occupies space; "physicists study both the nature of matter and the forces which govern it"

nodes.name: food
nodes.gloss: any substance that can be metabolized by an animal to give energy and build tissue

nodes.name: artifact
nodes.gloss: a man-made object taken as a whole

nodes.name: article
nodes.gloss: one of a class of artifacts; "an article of clothing"

nodes.name: psychological feature
nodes.gloss: a feature of the mental life of a living organism

nodes.name: cognition
nodes.gloss: the psychological result of perception and learning and reasoning

nodes.name: attribute
nodes.gloss: an abstraction belonging to or characteristic of an entity

nodes.name: location
nodes.gloss: a point or extent in space

nodes.name: shape
nodes.gloss: the spatial arrangement of something as distinct from its substance; "geometry is the mathematical science of shape"

nodes.name: group
nodes.gloss: any number of entities (members) considered as a unit

nodes.name: communication
nodes.gloss: something that is communicated by or to or between people or groups

nodes.name: microorganism
nodes.gloss: any organism of microscopic size

nodes.name: phytoplankton
nodes.gloss: photosynthetic or plant constituent of plankton; mainly unicellular algae

nodes.name: planktonic algae
nodes.gloss: unicellular algae

nodes.name: protoctist
nodes.gloss: any of the unicellular protists

nodes.name: alga
nodes.gloss: primitive chlorophyll-containing mainly aquatic eukaryotic organisms lacking true stems and roots and leaves

nodes.name: diatom
nodes.gloss: microscopic unicellular marine or freshwater colonial alga having cell walls impregnated with silica

nodes.name: soft-finned fish
nodes.gloss: any fish of the superorder Malacopterygii

nodes.name: cypriniform fish
nodes.gloss: a soft-finned fish of the order Cypriniformes

nodes.name: cyprinid
nodes.gloss: soft-finned mainly freshwater fishes typically having toothless jaws and cycloid scales

nodes.name: tench
nodes.gloss: freshwater dace-like game fish of Europe and western Asia noted for ability to survive outside water

nodes.name: goldfish
nodes.gloss: small golden or orange-red freshwater fishes of Eurasia used as pond or aquarium fishes

nodes.name: chordate
nodes.gloss: any animal of the phylum Chordata having a notochord or spinal column

nodes.name: vertebrate
nodes.gloss: animals having a bony or cartilaginous skeleton with a segmented spinal column and a large brain enclosed in a skull or cranium

nodes.name: aquatic vertebrate
nodes.gloss: animal living wholly or chiefly in or on water

nodes.name: cartilaginous fish
nodes.gloss: fishes in which the skeleton may be calcified but not ossified

nodes.name: elasmobranch
nodes.gloss: any of numerous fishes of the class Chondrichthyes characterized by a cartilaginous skeleton and placoid scales: sharks; rays; skates

nodes.name: shark
nodes.gloss: any of numerous elongate mostly marine carnivorous fishes with heterocercal caudal fins and tough skin covered with small toothlike scales

nodes.name: mackerel shark
nodes.gloss: fierce pelagic and oceanic sharks

nodes.name: great white shark
nodes.gloss: large aggressive shark widespread in warm seas; known to attack humans

nodes.name: requiem shark
nodes.gloss: any of numerous sharks from small relatively harmless bottom-dwellers to large dangerous oceanic and coastal species

nodes.name: tiger shark
nodes.gloss: large dangerous warm-water shark with striped or spotted body

nodes.name: hammerhead
nodes.gloss: medium-sized live-bearing shark with eyes at either end of a flattened hammer-shaped head; worldwide in warm waters; can be dangerous

nodes.name: ray
nodes.gloss: cartilaginous fishes having horizontally flattened bodies and enlarged winglike pectoral fins with gills on the underside; most swim by moving the pectoral fins

nodes.name: electric ray
nodes.gloss: any sluggish bottom-dwelling ray of the order Torpediniformes having a rounded body and electric organs on each side of the head capable of emitting strong electric discharges

nodes.name: stingray
nodes.gloss: large venomous ray with large barbed spines near the base of a thin whiplike tail capable of inflicting severe wounds

nodes.name: bird
nodes.gloss: warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrates characterized by feathers and forelimbs modified as wings

nodes.name: cock
nodes.gloss: adult male bird

nodes.name: hen
nodes.gloss: adult female bird

nodes.name: ratite
nodes.gloss: flightless birds having flat breastbones lacking a keel for attachment of flight muscles: ostriches; cassowaries; emus; moas; rheas; kiwis; elephant birds

nodes.name: ostrich
nodes.gloss: fast-running African flightless bird with two-toed feet; largest living bird

nodes.name: passerine
nodes.gloss: perching birds mostly small and living near the ground with feet having 4 toes arranged to allow for gripping the perch; most are songbirds; hatchlings are helpless

nodes.name: oscine
nodes.gloss: passerine bird having specialized vocal apparatus

nodes.name: finch
nodes.gloss: any of numerous small songbirds with short stout bills adapted for crushing seeds

nodes.name: brambling
nodes.gloss: Eurasian finch

nodes.name: goldfinch
nodes.gloss: small European finch having a crimson face and yellow-and-black wings

nodes.name: house finch
nodes.gloss: small finch originally of the western United States and Mexico

nodes.name: junco
nodes.gloss: small North American finch seen chiefly in winter

nodes.name: bunting
nodes.gloss: any of numerous seed-eating songbirds of Europe or North America

nodes.name: indigo bunting
nodes.gloss: small deep blue North American bunting

nodes.name: thrush
nodes.gloss: songbirds characteristically having brownish upper plumage with a spotted breast

nodes.name: robin
nodes.gloss: large American thrush having a rust-red breast and abdomen

nodes.name: nightingale
nodes.gloss: European songbird noted for its melodious nocturnal song

nodes.name: bulbul
nodes.gloss: nightingale spoken of in Persian poetry

nodes.name: corvine bird
nodes.gloss: birds of the crow family

nodes.name: jay
nodes.gloss: crested largely blue bird

nodes.name: magpie
nodes.gloss: long-tailed black-and-white crow that utters a raucous chattering call

nodes.name: titmouse
nodes.gloss: small insectivorous birds

nodes.name: chickadee
nodes.gloss: any of various small grey-and-black songbirds of North America

nodes.name: water ouzel
nodes.gloss: small stocky diving bird without webbed feet; frequents fast-flowing streams and feeds along the bottom

nodes.name: bird of prey
nodes.gloss: any of numerous carnivorous birds that hunt and kill other animals

nodes.name: hawk
nodes.gloss: diurnal bird of prey typically having short rounded wings and a long tail

nodes.name: kite
nodes.gloss: any of several small graceful hawks of the family Accipitridae having long pointed wings and feeding on insects and small animals

nodes.name: eagle
nodes.gloss: any of various large keen-sighted diurnal birds of prey noted for their broad wings and strong soaring flight

nodes.name: bald eagle
nodes.gloss: a large eagle of North America that has a white head and dark wings and body

nodes.name: vulture
nodes.gloss: any of various large diurnal birds of prey having naked heads and weak claws and feeding chiefly on carrion

nodes.name: owl
nodes.gloss: nocturnal bird of prey with hawk-like beak and claws and large head with front-facing eyes

nodes.name: great grey owl
nodes.gloss: large dish-faced owl of northern North America and western Eurasia

nodes.name: amphibian
nodes.gloss: cold-blooded vertebrate typically living on land but breeding in water; aquatic larvae undergo metamorphosis into adult form

nodes.name: salamander
nodes.gloss: any of various typically terrestrial amphibians that resemble lizards and that return to water only to breed

nodes.name: European fire salamander
nodes.gloss: a kind of European salamander

nodes.name: newt
nodes.gloss: small usually bright-colored semiaquatic salamanders of North America and Europe and northern Asia

nodes.name: common newt
nodes.gloss: small semiaquatic salamander

nodes.name: eft
nodes.gloss: a newt in its terrestrial stage of development

nodes.name: ambystomid
nodes.gloss: small to moderate-sized terrestrial or semiaquatic New World salamander

nodes.name: spotted salamander
nodes.gloss: glossy black North American salamander with yellow spots

nodes.name: axolotl
nodes.gloss: larval salamander of mountain lakes of Mexico that usually lives without metamorphosing

nodes.name: frog
nodes.gloss: any of various tailless stout-bodied amphibians with long hind limbs for leaping; semiaquatic and terrestrial species

nodes.name: true frog
nodes.gloss: insectivorous usually semiaquatic web-footed amphibian with smooth moist skin and long hind legs

nodes.name: bullfrog
nodes.gloss: largest North American frog; highly aquatic with a deep-pitched voice

nodes.name: tree frog
nodes.gloss: any of various Old World arboreal frogs distinguished from true frogs by adhesive suckers on the toes

nodes.name: tailed frog
nodes.gloss: western North American frog with a taillike copulatory organ

nodes.name: reptile
nodes.gloss: any cold-blooded vertebrate of the class Reptilia including tortoises, turtles, snakes, lizards, alligators, crocodiles, and extinct forms

nodes.name: anapsid
nodes.gloss: primitive reptile having no opening in the temporal region of the skull; all extinct except turtles

nodes.name: diapsid
nodes.gloss: reptile having a pair of openings in the skull behind each eye

nodes.name: chelonian
nodes.gloss: a reptile of the order Chelonia

nodes.name: turtle
nodes.gloss: any of various aquatic and land reptiles having a bony shell and flipper-like limbs for swimming

nodes.name: sea turtle
nodes.gloss: any of various large turtles with limbs modified into flippers; widely distributed in warm seas

nodes.name: loggerhead
nodes.gloss: very large carnivorous sea turtle; wide-ranging in warm open seas

nodes.name: leatherback turtle
nodes.gloss: wide-ranging marine turtle with flexible leathery carapace; largest living turtle

nodes.name: mud turtle
nodes.gloss: bottom-dwelling freshwater turtle inhabiting muddy rivers of North America and Central America

nodes.name: terrapin
nodes.gloss: any of various edible North American web-footed turtles living in fresh or brackish water

nodes.name: box turtle
nodes.gloss: chiefly terrestrial turtle of North America; shell can be closed tightly

nodes.name: saurian
nodes.gloss: any of various reptiles of the suborder Sauria which includes lizards; in former classifications included also the crocodiles and dinosaurs

nodes.name: lizard
nodes.gloss: relatively long-bodied reptile with usually two pairs of legs and a tapering tail

nodes.name: gecko
nodes.gloss: any of various small chiefly tropical and usually nocturnal insectivorous terrestrial lizards typically with immovable eyelids; completely harmless

nodes.name: banded gecko
nodes.gloss: any of several geckos with dark bands across the body and differing from typical geckos in having movable eyelids; of United States southwest and Florida Gulf Coast

nodes.name: iguanid
nodes.gloss: lizards of the New World and Madagascar and some Pacific islands; typically having a long tail and bright throat patch in males

nodes.name: common iguana
nodes.gloss: large herbivorous tropical American arboreal lizards with a spiny crest along the back; used as human food in Central America and South America

nodes.name: anole
nodes.gloss: small arboreal tropical American insectivorous lizards with the ability to change skin color

nodes.name: teiid lizard
nodes.gloss: tropical New World lizard with a long tail and large rectangular scales on the belly and a long tail

nodes.name: whiptail
nodes.gloss: any of numerous very agile and alert New World lizards

nodes.name: agamid
nodes.gloss: a lizard of the family Agamidae

nodes.name: agama
nodes.gloss: small terrestrial lizard of warm regions of the Old World

nodes.name: frilled lizard
nodes.gloss: large arboreal insectivorous Australian lizard with a ruff of skin around the neck

nodes.name: anguid lizard
nodes.gloss: any of a small family of lizards widely distributed in warm areas; all are harmless and useful as destroyers of e.g. slugs and insects

nodes.name: alligator lizard
nodes.gloss: slim short-limbed lizard having a distinctive fold on each side that permits expansion; of western North America

nodes.name: venomous lizard
nodes.gloss: any of two or three large heavy-bodied lizards; only known venomous lizards

nodes.name: Gila monster
nodes.gloss: large orange and black lizard of southwestern United States; not dangerous unless molested

nodes.name: lacertid lizard
nodes.gloss: Old World terrestrial lizard

nodes.name: green lizard
nodes.gloss: a common Eurasian lizard about a foot long

nodes.name: chameleon
nodes.gloss: lizard of Africa and Madagascar able to change skin color and having a projectile tongue

nodes.name: African chameleon
nodes.gloss: a chameleon found in Africa

nodes.name: monitor
nodes.gloss: any of various large tropical carnivorous lizards of Africa and Asia and Australia; fabled to warn of crocodiles

nodes.name: dragon lizard
nodes.gloss: the largest lizard in the world (10 feet); found on Indonesian islands

nodes.name: archosaur
nodes.gloss: extinct reptiles including: dinosaurs; plesiosaurs; pterosaurs; ichthyosaurs; thecodonts

nodes.name: crocodilian reptile
nodes.gloss: extant archosaurian reptile

nodes.name: crocodile
nodes.gloss: large voracious aquatic reptile having a long snout with massive jaws and sharp teeth and a body covered with bony plates; of sluggish tropical waters

nodes.name: African crocodile
nodes.gloss: a dangerous crocodile widely distributed in Africa

nodes.name: alligator
nodes.gloss: either of two amphibious reptiles related to crocodiles but with shorter broader snouts

nodes.name: American alligator
nodes.gloss: large alligator of the southeastern United States

nodes.name: dinosaur
nodes.gloss: any of numerous extinct terrestrial reptiles of the Mesozoic era

nodes.name: ornithischian
nodes.gloss: herbivorous dinosaur with a pelvis like that of a bird

nodes.name: ceratopsian
nodes.gloss: any of several four-footed herbivorous dinosaurs with enormous beaked skulls; of the late Cretaceous in North America and Mongolia

nodes.name: triceratops
nodes.gloss: huge ceratopsian dinosaur having three horns and the neck heavily armored with a very solid frill

nodes.name: snake
nodes.gloss: limbless scaly elongate reptile; some are venomous

nodes.name: colubrid snake
nodes.gloss: mostly harmless temperate-to-tropical terrestrial or arboreal or aquatic snakes

nodes.name: thunder snake
nodes.gloss: small reddish wormlike snake of eastern United States

nodes.name: ringneck snake
nodes.gloss: any of numerous small nonvenomous North American snakes with a yellow or orange ring around the neck

nodes.name: hognose snake
nodes.gloss: harmless North American snake with upturned nose; may spread its head and neck or play dead when disturbed

nodes.name: green snake
nodes.gloss: either of two North American chiefly insectivorous snakes that are green in color

nodes.name: king snake
nodes.gloss: any of numerous nonvenomous North American constrictors; feed on other snakes and small mammals

nodes.name: garter snake
nodes.gloss: any of numerous nonvenomous longitudinally-striped viviparous North American and Central American snakes

nodes.name: water snake
nodes.gloss: any of various mostly harmless snakes that live in or near water

nodes.name: vine snake
nodes.gloss: slender arboreal snake found from southern Arizona to Bolivia

nodes.name: night snake
nodes.gloss: nocturnal prowler of western United States and Mexico

nodes.name: constrictor
nodes.gloss: any of various large nonvenomous snakes that kill their prey by crushing it in its coils

nodes.name: boa
nodes.gloss: any of several chiefly tropical constrictors with vestigial hind limbs

nodes.name: boa constrictor
nodes.gloss: very large boa of tropical America and West Indies

nodes.name: python
nodes.gloss: large Old World boas

nodes.name: rock python
nodes.gloss: very large python of tropical and southern Africa

nodes.name: elapid
nodes.gloss: any of numerous venomous fanged snakes of warmer parts of both hemispheres

nodes.name: cobra
nodes.gloss: venomous Asiatic and African elapid snakes that can expand the skin of the neck into a hood

nodes.name: Indian cobra
nodes.gloss: a cobra of tropical Africa and Asia

nodes.name: mamba
nodes.gloss: arboreal snake of central and southern Africa whose bite is often fatal

nodes.name: black mamba
nodes.gloss: a highly venomous southern African mamba dreaded because of its quickness and readiness to bite

nodes.name: green mamba
nodes.gloss: green phase of the black mamba

nodes.name: sea snake
nodes.gloss: any of numerous venomous aquatic viviparous snakes having a fin-like tail; of warm littoral seas; feed on fish which they immobilize with quick-acting venom

nodes.name: viper
nodes.gloss: venomous Old World snakes characterized by hollow venom-conducting fangs in the upper jaw

nodes.name: horned viper
nodes.gloss: highly venomous viper of northern Africa and southwestern Asia having a horny spine above each eye

nodes.name: pit viper
nodes.gloss: New World vipers with hollow fangs and a heat-sensitive pit on each side of the head

nodes.name: rattlesnake
nodes.gloss: pit viper with horny segments at the end of the tail that rattle when shaken

nodes.name: diamondback
nodes.gloss: large deadly rattlesnake with diamond-shaped markings

nodes.name: sidewinder
nodes.gloss: small pale-colored desert rattlesnake of southwestern United States; body moves in an s-shaped curve

nodes.name: carcase
nodes.gloss: the dead body of an animal especially one slaughtered and dressed for food

nodes.name: carrion
nodes.gloss: the dead and rotting body of an animal; unfit for human food

nodes.name: roadkill
nodes.gloss: the dead body of an animal that has been killed on a road by a vehicle; "vultures usually feed on carrion or roadkill"

nodes.name: arthropod
nodes.gloss: invertebrate having jointed limbs and a segmented body with an exoskeleton made of chitin

nodes.name: trilobite
nodes.gloss: an extinct arthropod that was abundant in Paleozoic times; had an exoskeleton divided into three parts

nodes.name: arachnid
nodes.gloss: air-breathing arthropods characterized by simple eyes and four pairs of legs

nodes.name: harvestman
nodes.gloss: spiderlike arachnid with a small rounded body and very long thin legs

nodes.name: scorpion
nodes.gloss: arachnid of warm dry regions having a long segmented tail ending in a venomous stinger

nodes.name: spider
nodes.gloss: predatory arachnid with eight legs, two poison fangs, two feelers, and usually two silk-spinning organs at the back end of the body; they spin silk to make cocoons for eggs or traps for prey

nodes.name: black and gold garden spider
nodes.gloss: a widely distributed North American garden spider

nodes.name: barn spider
nodes.gloss: an orange and tan spider with darkly banded legs that spins an orb web daily; "the barn spider was made famous in E. B. White's book `Charlotte's Web'"

nodes.name: garden spider
nodes.gloss: a spider common in European gardens

nodes.name: black widow
nodes.gloss: venomous New World spider; the female is black with an hourglass-shaped red mark on the underside of the abdomen

nodes.name: tarantula
nodes.gloss: large hairy tropical spider with fangs that can inflict painful but not highly venomous bites

nodes.name: wolf spider
nodes.gloss: ground spider that hunts its prey instead of using a web

nodes.name: acarine
nodes.gloss: mite or tick

nodes.name: tick
nodes.gloss: any of two families of small parasitic arachnids with barbed proboscis; feed on blood of warm-blooded animals

nodes.name: centipede
nodes.gloss: chiefly nocturnal predacious arthropod having a flattened body of 15 to 173 segments each with a pair of legs, the foremost pair being modified as prehensors

nodes.name: grouse
nodes.gloss: popular game bird having a plump body and feathered legs and feet

nodes.name: black grouse
nodes.gloss: grouse of which the male is bluish-black

nodes.name: ptarmigan
nodes.gloss: large Arctic and subarctic grouse with feathered feet and usually white winter plumage

nodes.name: ruffed grouse
nodes.gloss: valued as a game bird in eastern United States and Canada

nodes.name: prairie chicken
nodes.gloss: brown mottled North American grouse of western prairies

nodes.name: phasianid
nodes.gloss: a kind of game bird in the family Phasianidae

nodes.name: pheasant
nodes.gloss: large long-tailed gallinaceous bird native to the Old World but introduced elsewhere

nodes.name: peafowl
nodes.gloss: very large terrestrial southeast Asian pheasant often raised as an ornamental bird

nodes.name: peacock
nodes.gloss: male peafowl; having a crested head and very large fanlike tail marked with iridescent eyes or spots

nodes.name: quail
nodes.gloss: small gallinaceous game birds

nodes.name: partridge
nodes.gloss: small Old World gallinaceous game birds

nodes.name: parrot
nodes.gloss: usually brightly colored zygodactyl tropical birds with short hooked beaks and the ability to mimic sounds

nodes.name: African grey
nodes.gloss: commonly domesticated grey parrot with red-and-black tail and white face; native to equatorial Africa

nodes.name: macaw
nodes.gloss: long-tailed brilliantly colored parrot of Central America and South America; among the largest and showiest of parrots

nodes.name: cockatoo
nodes.gloss: white or light-colored crested parrot of the Australian region; often kept as cage birds

nodes.name: sulphur-crested cockatoo
nodes.gloss: white cockatoo with a yellow erectile crest

nodes.name: lory
nodes.gloss: small brightly colored Australasian parrots having a brush-tipped tongue for feeding on nectar and soft fruits

nodes.name: lorikeet
nodes.gloss: any of various small lories

nodes.name: cuculiform bird
nodes.gloss: birds having zygodactyl feet (except for the touracos)

nodes.name: cuckoo
nodes.gloss: any of numerous European and North American birds having pointed wings and a long tail

nodes.name: coucal
nodes.gloss: Old World ground-living cuckoo having a long dagger-like hind claw

nodes.name: coraciiform bird
nodes.gloss: chiefly short-legged arboreal nonpasserine birds that nest in holes

nodes.name: bee eater
nodes.gloss: colorful chiefly tropical Old World bird having a strong graceful flight; feeds on especially bees

nodes.name: hornbill
nodes.gloss: bird of tropical Africa and Asia having a very large bill surmounted by a bony protuberance; related to kingfishers

nodes.name: apodiform bird
nodes.gloss: nonpasserine bird having long wings and weak feet; spends much of its time in flight

nodes.name: hummingbird
nodes.gloss: tiny American bird having brilliant iridescent plumage and long slender bills; wings are specialized for vibrating flight

nodes.name: piciform bird
nodes.gloss: any of numerous nonpasserine insectivorous climbing birds usually having strong bills for boring wood

nodes.name: jacamar
nodes.gloss: tropical American insectivorous bird having a long sharp bill and iridescent green or bronze plumage

nodes.name: toucan
nodes.gloss: brilliantly colored arboreal fruit-eating bird of tropical America having a very large thin-walled beak

nodes.name: aquatic bird
nodes.gloss: wading and swimming and diving birds of either fresh or salt water

nodes.name: waterfowl
nodes.gloss: freshwater aquatic bird

nodes.name: anseriform bird
nodes.gloss: chiefly web-footed swimming birds

nodes.name: duck
nodes.gloss: small wild or domesticated web-footed broad-billed swimming bird usually having a depressed body and short legs

nodes.name: drake
nodes.gloss: adult male of a wild or domestic duck

nodes.name: sea duck
nodes.gloss: any of various large diving ducks found along the seacoast: eider; scoter; merganser

nodes.name: merganser
nodes.gloss: large crested fish-eating diving duck having a slender hooked bill with serrated edges

nodes.name: red-breasted merganser
nodes.gloss: widely distributed merganser of America and Europe

nodes.name: goose
nodes.gloss: web-footed long-necked typically gregarious migratory aquatic birds usually larger and less aquatic than ducks

nodes.name: swan
nodes.gloss: stately heavy-bodied aquatic bird with very long neck and usually white plumage as adult

nodes.name: black swan
nodes.gloss: large Australian swan having black plumage and a red bill

nodes.name: mammal
nodes.gloss: any warm-blooded vertebrate having the skin more or less covered with hair; young are born alive except for the small subclass of monotremes and nourished with milk

nodes.name: tusker
nodes.gloss: any mammal with prominent tusks (especially an elephant or wild boar)

nodes.name: prototherian
nodes.gloss: primitive oviparous mammals found only in Australia and Tasmania and New Guinea

nodes.name: monotreme
nodes.gloss: the most primitive mammals comprising the only extant members of the subclass Prototheria

nodes.name: echidna
nodes.gloss: a burrowing monotreme mammal covered with spines and having a long snout and claws for hunting ants and termites; native to Australia

nodes.name: platypus
nodes.gloss: small densely furred aquatic monotreme of Australia and Tasmania having a broad bill and tail and webbed feet; only species in the family Ornithorhynchidae

nodes.name: metatherian
nodes.gloss: primitive pouched mammals found mainly in Australia and the Americas

nodes.name: marsupial
nodes.gloss: mammals of which the females have a pouch (the marsupium) containing the teats where the young are fed and carried

nodes.name: kangaroo
nodes.gloss: any of several herbivorous leaping marsupials of Australia and New Guinea having large powerful hind legs and a long thick tail

nodes.name: wallaby
nodes.gloss: any of various small or medium-sized kangaroos; often brightly colored

nodes.name: phalanger
nodes.gloss: small furry Australian arboreal marsupials having long usually prehensile tails

nodes.name: koala
nodes.gloss: sluggish tailless Australian arboreal marsupial with grey furry ears and coat; feeds on eucalyptus leaves and bark

nodes.name: wombat
nodes.gloss: burrowing herbivorous Australian marsupials about the size of a badger

nodes.name: placental
nodes.gloss: mammals having a placenta; all mammals except monotremes and marsupials

nodes.name: scale
nodes.gloss: a flattened rigid plate forming part of the body covering of many animals

nodes.name: shell
nodes.gloss: the hard largely calcareous covering of a mollusc or a brachiopod

nodes.name: test
nodes.gloss: a hard outer covering as of some amoebas and sea urchins

nodes.name: invertebrate
nodes.gloss: any animal lacking a backbone or notochord; the term is not used as a scientific classification

nodes.name: coelenterate
nodes.gloss: radially symmetrical animals having saclike bodies with only one opening and tentacles with stinging structures; they occur in polyp and medusa forms

nodes.name: jellyfish
nodes.gloss: any of numerous usually marine and free-swimming coelenterates that constitute the sexually reproductive forms of hydrozoans and scyphozoans

nodes.name: anthozoan
nodes.gloss: sessile marine coelenterates including solitary and colonial polyps; the medusoid phase is entirely suppressed

nodes.name: sea anemone
nodes.gloss: marine polyps that resemble flowers but have oral rings of tentacles; differ from corals in forming no hard skeleton

nodes.name: coral
nodes.gloss: marine colonial polyp characterized by a calcareous skeleton; masses in a variety of shapes often forming reefs

nodes.name: stony coral
nodes.gloss: corals having calcareous skeletons aggregations of which form reefs and islands

nodes.name: brain coral
nodes.gloss: massive reef-building coral having a convoluted and furrowed surface

nodes.name: worm

nodes.gloss: a plant having foliage that is shed annually at the end of the growing season

nodes.name: poisonous plant
nodes.gloss: a plant that when touched or ingested in sufficient quantity can be harmful or fatal to an organism

nodes.name: vine
nodes.gloss: a plant with a weak stem that derives support from climbing, twining, or creeping along a surface

nodes.name: climber
nodes.gloss: a vine or climbing plant that readily grows up a support or over other plants

nodes.name: creeper
nodes.gloss: any plant (as ivy or periwinkle) that grows by creeping

nodes.name: tendril
nodes.gloss: slender stem-like structure by which some twining plants attach themselves to an object for support

nodes.name: woody plant
nodes.gloss: a plant having hard lignified tissues or woody parts especially stems

nodes.name: lignosae
nodes.gloss: a category in some early taxonomies

nodes.name: arborescent plant
nodes.gloss: having the shape or characteristics of a tree

nodes.name: tree
nodes.gloss: a tall perennial woody plant having a main trunk and branches forming a distinct elevated crown; includes both gymnosperms and angiosperms

nodes.name: stump
nodes.gloss: the base part of a tree that remains standing after the tree has been felled

nodes.name: shrub
nodes.gloss: a low woody perennial plant usually having several major stems

nodes.name: bramble
nodes.gloss: any of various rough thorny shrubs or vines

nodes.name: liana
nodes.gloss: a woody climbing usually tropical plant

nodes.name: geophyte
nodes.gloss: a perennial plant that propagates by underground bulbs or tubers or corms

nodes.name: desert plant
nodes.gloss: plant adapted for life with a limited supply of water; compare hydrophyte and mesophyte

nodes.name: mesophyte
nodes.gloss: land plant growing in surroundings having an average supply of water; compare xerophyte and hydrophyte

nodes.name: aquatic plant
nodes.gloss: a plant that grows partly or wholly in water whether rooted in the mud, as a lotus, or floating without anchorage, as the water hyacinth

nodes.name: marsh plant
nodes.gloss: a semiaquatic plant that grows in soft wet land; most are monocots: sedge, sphagnum, grasses, cattails, etc; possibly heath

nodes.name: air plant
nodes.gloss: plant that derives moisture and nutrients from the air and rain; usually grows on another plant but not parasitic on it

nodes.name: hemiepiphyte
nodes.gloss: a plant that is an epiphyte for part of its life

nodes.name: strangler
nodes.gloss: an epiphytic vine or tree whose aerial roots extend down the trunk of a supporting tree and coalesce around it eventually strangling the tree

nodes.name: rock plant
nodes.gloss: plant that grows on or among rocks or is suitable for a rock garden

nodes.name: lithophyte
nodes.gloss: plant that grows on rocks or stony soil and derives nourishment from the atmosphere

nodes.name: rupestral plant
nodes.gloss: plants growing among rocks

nodes.name: autophyte
nodes.gloss: plant capable of synthesizing its own food from simple organic substances

nodes.name: root crop
nodes.gloss: crop grown for its enlarged roots: e.g. beets; potatoes; turnips

nodes.name: prophyll
nodes.gloss: a plant structure resembling a leaf

nodes.name: stock
nodes.gloss: a plant or stem onto which a graft is made; especially a plant grown specifically to provide the root part of grafted plants

nodes.name: tuberous plant
nodes.gloss: plant growing from a tuber

nodes.name: receptacle
nodes.gloss: enlarged tip of a stem that bears the floral parts

nodes.name: ear
nodes.gloss: fruiting spike of a cereal plant especially corn

nodes.name: bulbous plant
nodes.gloss: plant growing from a bulb

nodes.name: cormous plant
nodes.gloss: plant growing from a corm

nodes.name: fruit
nodes.gloss: the ripened reproductive body of a seed plant

nodes.name: seed
nodes.gloss: a small hard fruit

nodes.name: kernel
nodes.gloss: the inner and usually edible part of a seed or grain or nut or fruit stone; "black walnut kernels are difficult to get out of the shell"

nodes.name: grape
nodes.gloss: any of numerous woody vines of genus Vitis bearing clusters of edible berries

nodes.name: Boston ivy
nodes.gloss: Asiatic vine with three-lobed leaves and purple berries

nodes.name: woodbine
nodes.gloss: common North American vine with compound leaves and bluish-black berrylike fruit

nodes.name: true pepper
nodes.gloss: any of various shrubby vines of the genus Piper

nodes.name: peperomia
nodes.gloss: any of various plants of the genus Peperomia; grown primarily for their often succulent foliage

nodes.name: yerba mansa
nodes.gloss: stoloniferous herb of southwestern United States and Mexico having a pungent rootstock and small spicate flowers with white bracts suggesting an anemone

nodes.name: lobe
nodes.gloss: (botany) a part into which a leaf is divided

nodes.name: ligule
nodes.gloss: (botany) any appendage to a plant that is shaped like a strap

nodes.name: bark
nodes.gloss: tough protective covering of the woody stems and roots of trees and other woody plants

nodes.name: myrmecophyte
nodes.gloss: plant that affords shelter or food to ants that live in symbiotic relations with it

nodes.name: psilophyte
nodes.gloss: any plant of the order Psilophytales: a savannah plant

nodes.name: psilophyton
nodes.gloss: any plant or fossil of the genus Psilophyton

nodes.name: asclepiad
nodes.gloss: any plant of the family Asclepiadaceae

nodes.name: milkweed
nodes.gloss: any of numerous plants of the genus Asclepias having milky juice and pods that split open releasing seeds with downy tufts

nodes.name: cruel plant
nodes.gloss: robust twining shrub having racemes of fragrant white or pink flowers with flat spreading terminal petals that trap nocturnal moths and hold them until dawn

nodes.name: hoya
nodes.gloss: any plant of the genus Hoya having fleshy leaves and usually nectariferous flowers

nodes.name: silk vine
nodes.gloss: deciduous climber for arches and fences having ill-scented but interesting flowers and poisonous yellow fruits; cultivated for its dark shining foliage; southeastern Europe to Asia Minor

nodes.name: soma
nodes.gloss: leafless East Indian vine; its sour milky juice formerly used to make an intoxicating drink

nodes.name: stapelia
nodes.gloss: any of various plants of the genus Stapelia having succulent leafless toothed stems resembling cacti and large foul-smelling (often star-shaped) flowers

nodes.name: negro vine
nodes.gloss: twining vine with hairy foliage and dark purplish-brown flowers

nodes.name: round shape
nodes.gloss: a shape that is curved and without sharp angles

nodes.name: sphere
nodes.gloss: a solid figure bounded by a spherical surface (including the space it encloses)

nodes.name: ball
nodes.gloss: an object with a spherical shape; "a ball of fire"

nodes.name: material
nodes.gloss: the tangible substance that goes into the makeup of a physical object; "coal is a hard black material"; "wheat is the stuff they use to make bread"

nodes.name: paper
nodes.gloss: a material made of cellulose pulp derived mainly from wood or rags or certain grasses

nodes.name: tissue
nodes.gloss: a soft thin (usually translucent) paper

nodes.name: toilet tissue
nodes.gloss: a soft thin absorbent paper for use in toilets

nodes.name: biological clock
nodes.gloss: an innate mechanism in living organisms that controls the periodicity of many physiological functions
